html:
Paris is the capital and largest city of France, on the river Seine. For most of the last thousand years it has been the seat of French government, and for long stretches one of Europe's leading centres of learning, art and fashion.

It began as a settlement of the Gallic Parisii on the Île de la Cité, which the Romans called Lutetia. Clovis, king of the Franks, made it his capital around 508, and from 987 the Capetian kings built their power from it. In the 1100s and 1200s it gained the Gothic cathedral of Notre-Dame and the University of Paris, the great school of theology of medieval Europe.

The French Revolution began in its streets with the storming of the Bastille in 1789, and Napoleon ruled his empire from it. Under Napoleon III, Haussmann's rebuilding of 1853 to 1870 cut wide boulevards through the old city. In 1871 the radical Paris Commune held the city for two months before the army crushed it.

From the late 1800s Paris was a magnet for artists. The Impressionists painted its streets and cafés, the Eiffel Tower rose for the fair of 1889, and painters such as Picasso found new ideas there, among them African masks. German troops occupied it from 1940 to 1944.
sum: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, on the river Seine. For most of the last thousand years it has been the seat of French government, and for long stretches one of Europe's leading centres of learning, art and fashion.
